A highly visible tornado that came to be known as the Andover Tornado initially touched down in rural Sedgwick county and tracked to the east northeast into Butler county, Kansas. Two direct injuries occurred, when a manufactured home was completely destroyed, with two occupants inside. Two people were transported to local hospitals with serious injuries.  Total structures affected were 116, with 22 of those being homes.  The rest of the structures affected were barns, sheds, detached garages, etc. This tornado crossed the county line into Butler County. Damage were estimated at  4.5 million dollars.

A highly visible tornado tracked across portions of Andover, Kansas, during the early evening hours of April 29th, 2022. The tornado went through a highly populated portion of town, including 2 different subdivisions. Also a health club took a direct hit, but no injuries occurred due to actions taken by the health club. Only 1 direct injury occurred from the tornado, with 3 indirect injuries occurred during search and rescue operations. Total damaged house or destroyed structures in Andover and rural Butler County were 205. Of the damaged properties, approximately 180 were residences and the rest were businesses or city buildings. Damage estimates were around $37 million.

Precipitation transitioned to snow around 5AM which continued to fall through the day. Moderate to heavy snow with strong northwest winds led to reduced visibilities and blizzard conditions across the county starting at 7:30AM until mid day. Winds had sustained speeds of 20 to near 30 mph with gusts of 40 to 45 mph. Snow continued to fall until 4:30PM. The storm total snowfalls ranged from 3 to near 5 inches with the highest report of 4.5 inches at McConnell Air Force Base.

Salina Regional Airport reported blizzard conditions starting in the morning and continuing into the afternoon. The combination of moderate to heavy snow and strong northwest winds led to blizzard conditions for nearly six hours. A peak wind gust of 58 mph was reported at 9:33AM. The highest snowfall total was reported in Salina by law enforcement at around 12 inches.

A long duration winter storm event impacted the area which started as drizzle and freezing drizzle followed by freezing rain and sleet before transitioning to snow. Colonel Jabara Airport measured a flat ice accumulation of 0.45 inches. Storm total snowfalls ranged from 3 to 5 inches. Visibilities were reduced to under a mile after the blizzard conditions which ended around 1PM in eastern portions of the county and lasted through 5PM on the 5th. The accumulated ice followed by snow created a mess on the roadways and several slide offs along with other vehicular accidents occurred during the event. Unfortunately there were two fatalities from one of the accidents at the tail end of the event.

There were some slide offs along with other vehicular accidents occurred during the event with no known injuries.

The full transition to snow occurred just before 10AM on the 5th based on the observations from the Chanute Martin Johnson Airport. The storm total flat ice accumulation based on the airport sensor was 0.33 of an inch which was combined with sustained winds around 15 mph which increased closer to 20 mph in the afternoon of the 5th. There is at least one known vehicular accident during the morning of the 5th with no apparent injuries.

This was a long duration winter event which started as freezing drizzle during the morning of the 4th then changed to freezing rain and sleet before fully transitioning over to snow in the morning on the 5th. Emergency management measured 0.47 of an inch of ice on shrubs and estimated 4 to 8 inches of snow across the county. There were a few vehicular accidents on the Kansas Turnpike during the morning hours of the 4th with no apparent injuries.

A long duration winter storm event impacted the area which started as drizzle and freezing drizzle followed by freezing rain and sleet before transitioning to snow. A measured a flat ice accumulation of 0.47 inches was reported from the freezing drizzle and freezing rain at the Salina Municipal Airport. Storm total snowfall amounts ranged from 6 to 12 inches with the highest amounts along the Interstate 70 corridor near Salina according to CoCoRaHS and law enforcement reports. Visibilities were reduced to under a mile after the blizzard conditions through around 5PM on the 5th. The accumulated ice followed by snow created a mess on the roadways, and several slide offs or other vehicular accidents occurred during the event; there was one possible injury in one accident.

A long duration winter storm event impacted the area which started as freezing drizzle as well as freezing rain and snow with some sleet mixed in. The storm total snowfalls ranged from 8 to an estimated 15 inches of snow by law enforcement. There were some slide offs that occurred during the morning of the 4th with no known injuries.

A long duration winter storm event impacted the area which started as freezing drizzle as well as freezing rain and snow with some sleet mixed in. The storm total snowfalls ranged from 7 to 10 inches with the highest values in the southeast quadrant of the county. There were a couple slide offs along that occurred during the morning of the 4th with no known injuries.

A long duration winter storm event impacted the area which started as freezing drizzle which transitioned to snow with maybe some sleet mixed in. The estimated storm total snowfall was 10 inches of snow by law enforcement. There a couple some slide offs that occurred during the morning of the 5th with no known injuries.

A long duration winter storm event impacted the area which started as freezing drizzle as well as freezing rain before mixing in snow. The storm total snowfalls ranged from 3.5 inches in the southwest corner about seven miles southwest of McPherson to 11 inches in Lindsborg. There were some slide offs that occurred during the morning of the 4th with no known injuries.

A long duration winter storm event impacted the area which started as freezing drizzle with a transition to snow and some sleet mixed in. The storm total snowfalls ranged from 8 inches in the southwest corner of the county to 10 inches in Hillsboro. Slick roadways resulted after the freezing drizzle. No known injury accidents were reported.

A long duration winter storm event impacted the area which started as freezing drizzle in the morning of the 4th which transitioned to snow by the morning of the 5th. The storm total snowfalls ranged from 2 to 5 inches with the highest value in the northwest corner six miles east of Whitewater. There were some slide offs along with other vehicular accidents that occurred during the event with no known injuries.

A combination of freezing drizzle and freezing rain resulted in a storm total ice accretion at 0.5 of an inch which was measured by the emergency manager on shrub branches. The winds were around 15 mph during this accumulation. Roadways were slick, but no known injury accidents were reported.

A long duration winter storm event impacted the area which started as freezing drizzle as well as freezing rain then sleet mixed in before transitioning over to snow. A Cooperative Observer in Kingman reported 0.8 of an inch of ice and sleet accumulation. Storm total snowfalls in the northern portion of the county were around 4 inches. The highest snowfall total was a public report in Kingman of 5 to 6 inches.

Russell Municipal Airport had an increase in snow intensity in combination with the winds starting in the early morning hours with blizzard conditions reported for about 10 hours. Sustained northerly winds had speeds of 20 to 30 mph for this period. The peak wind gust was 49 mph which occurred at 11:35AM. Many roadways were closed due to the conditions and drifting snow.

Lyons Rice County Municipal Airport had an increase in snow intensity in combination with the winds starting in the morning hours with blizzard conditions reported for about eight hours. Many roadways were closed due to the conditions and drifting snow.

Hutchinson Municipal Airport had an increase in snow intensity in combination with the winds starting in the morning hours with blizzard conditions reported for five hours. Sustained northerly winds had speeds of 15 to 25 mph for this period. The peak wind gust was 51 mph which occurred at 9:28AM.

There was hazardous travel on many roadways in part due to drifting snow. Ambulances and other vehicles got stuck in snow drifts during this event.

Based on the NWS storm survey, the tornado started in Pratt County then went into Stafford County before entering western Reno County. The total track of the tornado was around 32 miles with 21 of those in Reno County. A peak of EF3 damage was found with estimated winds of 155 mph occurring in Stafford and Pratt counties. In Reno County, the peak estimated winds were 145 mph based on a brick exterior home that had all of the exterior walls removed except long entryway. One portion of an interior wall remained. The maximum width was around one mile. This tornado damaged multiple homes to varying degrees in the town of Plevna with damage ranging from EF0 to EF2. Then the torando tracked northeast before going northwest prior to dissipating.

Numerous reports of significant flash flooding were reported across portions of Butler County. These reports included, but not limited to, the following road closures: Kansas Highway 77 at McCollum, Highway 254 in El Dorado and Prairie Creek Road near Benton. Many other side streets and roads across Butler County were also impassible especially in El Dorado. In addition to the road closures, numerous reports of stalled vehicles due to high water were reported across many areas of the county. Homes were  evacuated on the north and southwest side of El Dorado due to rapidly rising flood waters. Flooding on area roadways and into homes impacted the Wagon Wheel neighborhood near Santa Fe Lake. A total of 240 homes and businesses were impacted in the county with damage to county roadways as well resulting in $4 million infrastructure damages.

Russell Municipal Airport measured sustained wind speeds of 33 to 40 mph with two gusts of 58 mph over a 15 minute window.

The ASOS site at Russell Municipal Airport had numerous issues reporting data during the day, so data was incomplete through the event. However, there were several recorded gusts between 58 and 62 mph between 5 AM CDT to 4 PM CDT before the site stopped reporting altogether. Based on surrounding reports, high winds likely ended around 5 PM CDT.

There was a peak wind gust of 58 mph at the Kansas Mesonet Site about 1 mile northwest of Denmark. Based on surrounding observations and reports, high winds likely occurred between 6 AM CDT and 5 PM CDT.

The ASOS site at Salina Regional Airport recorded multiple and consistent gusts between 58 and 61 mph between 7 AM CDT and 6 PM CDT. The site also recorded sustained winds of at least 40 mph between 12 PM CDT and 3 PM CDT. Lastly, the strongest wind gust measured in the county was 63 mph at 11:45 AM CDT from a KDOT site about 5 miles north-northwest of Salina.

A KS-DOT site about 7 miles south-southwest of Westfall measured a wind gust of 62 mph at 9:10 AM CDT, then a 62-mph gust was measured at a Union Pacific site about 6 miles east-northeast of Kanopolis. Meanwhile, the AWOS site at Ellsworth Municipal Airport recorded sustained winds of at least 40 mph between 1 PM CDT and 6 PM CDT.

The peak wind gusts at the AWOS site near Great Bend Municipal Airport were 59 mph at 1:10 PM CDT and 60 mph at 4:27 PM CDT. Additionally, the site recorded sustained winds in excess of 40 mph between 10 AM CDT and 6 PM CDT.

The AWOS site at Lyons-Rice County Municipal Airport recorded sustained winds of at least 40 mph between 10 AM CDT and 7 PM CDT. The peak sustained winds were 44 mph recorded at 4:55 PM CDT. The peak wind gust across the county was 56 mph recorded by a Kansas Mesonet 2 miles west Little River.

A Union Pacific site 1 mile west of Canton began measuring wind gusts in excess of 58 mph beginning at 7 AM CDT, and the peak gust at this site was 65 mph at 8:43 AM CDT. Meanwhile, the AWOS site at McPherson Airport measured sustained winds in excess of 40 mph between 10 AM CDT and 6 PM CDT.

The ASOS site at Hutchinson Regional Airport measured wind gusts in excess of 58 mph with the peak gust of 61 mph occurring at 11:52 AM CDT. It should be noted that the site had issues reporting throughout the day, so the data is incomplete. A Union Pacific site recorded a wind gust of 59 mph at 5:19 PM CDT. Based on these reports and reports surrounding Reno County, high winds likely occurred between 10 AM CDT and 6 PM CDT.

The first report of a powerline being knocked down occurred at 8:44 AM CDT. Meanwhile, the AWOS site began reporting sustained winds in excess of 40 mph around the same time. These sustained winds persisted until 6 PM CDT, and at least 3 more reports of powerlines being knocked down by strong winds were reported throughout the county in this time frame. Lastly, the AWOS site also recorded wind gusts in excess of 58 mph between 10 AM CDT and 6 PM CDT with the peak gust of 62 mph occurring at 11:09 AM CDT.

The ASOS site at Eisenhower National Airport began recorded periodic wind gusts in excess of 58 mph along with periods of sustained winds in excess of 40 mph between 10 AM CDT and 7 PM CDT. The peak wind gust was 63 mph at 1107 AM CDT. Additional wind gusts over 58 mph were noted at Jabara Airport along with a couple of personal weather stations across the county.

A personal weather station located about 3 miles northwest of Wellington measured a peak wind gust of 58 mph at 3:36 PM CDT. Additionally, the AWOS site at Wellington Municipal Airport measured sustained winds in excess of 40 mph between 10 AM CDT and 6:30 PM CDT with the peak sustained wind of 41 mph occurring multiple times in this time frame.

The AWOS site at Anthony Municipal Airport measured a peak wind gust of 59 mph at 6:32 PM CDT. Additionally, sustained winds in excess of 40 mph were measured between 10 AM CDT and 7 PM CDT with the peak sustained wind of 44 mph at 10:15 AM CDT.
The AWOS site at Kingman-Clyde Cessna Airport measured sustained winds in excess of 40 mph between 10 AM CDT and 7 PM CDT. The peak sustained wind of 44 mph was measured at 10:23 AM CDT.

The ASOS site at Strother Field measured sustained winds in excess of 40 mph a few times between 1 PM CDT and 7:30 PM CDT. The peak sustained wind of 41 mph was measured at 1:05 PM CDT and 2:20 PM CDT.

A personal weather station in Madison recorded a wind gust of 59 mph at 2:59 PM CDT. Additionally, the AWOS site at Eureka Municipal Airport measured sustained winds in excess of 40 mph between 9:30 AM CDT and 4:30 PM CDT. The peak sustained wind gust of 43 mph was measured at 9:55 AM CDT and 3:55 PM CDT.
A personal weather station near Benton measured a 60 mph wind gust at 11:37 AM CDT. This was around the same time as a 61 mph wind gust measured at Jabara Airport.

After rounds of showers and thunderstorms, dought conditions went from severe (D2) to moderate (D1) early in the month. Conditions further improved in the latter part of the month to abnormally dry (D0) and even none in the northeast corner.

While severe drought conditions (D2) started the month, there were rounds of showers and thunderstorms to improve the status through the month. All but a sliver in a far southern portion of the county improved to moderate drought (D1) in the first week of the month. This sliver dropped to moderate drought on the 21st while the rest of the county further improved to abnormally dry (D0). At the end of the month, the northeast third had their drought status removed completely. There was a range of 4.6 to 10.2 inches of rain that feel in the first 21 days of the month according to CoCoRaHS and cooperative observer reports.

The eastern third of the county improved to moderate drought (D1) in the first week of the month. In the far northern and eastern portions of the county, the area recovered further with the status in the abnormally dry (D0) category by the end of the month.

The southeast third of the county entered into severe drought conditions (D2) at the very start of the month with the middle third being in moderate drought conditions (D1) and the northwest corner in abnormally dry conditions (D0). Showers and thunderstorms helped to improve the southeast quadrant on the 21st with the southern third of the county in moderate drought (D1) while the rest of the county was abnormally dry (D0) for the remainder of the month.

The month started with the southeast quadrant of the county in severe drought conditions (D2) while the rest of the county was in moderate drought (D1). Showers and thunderstorms in the first week of the month helped the far southeast corner leaving only south central portions of the county in severe drought (D2) on the 7th and lasting until the 21st. This segment went to moderate drought (D1) before getting even better by reaching the abnormally dry (D0) category at the end of the month joining most of the rest of the county. The far northeast corner eliminated their drought status at the end of the month.

Water covered the road for a good portion of the day on Highway 77 north of El Dorado.

Water ran over numerous roads across the county.  Fast runnnig water covered the road along Highway 81 west of Belle Plaine and also south of Belle Plaine on Oliver near 60th Avenue.  A water rescue was performed at 60th Avenue when a pickup truck tried to drive through 2 feet deep water and became stranded when his truck was pushed off the road.  A local resident with an airboat helped in the rescue.

Interstate 35 (The Kansas Turnpike) was closed due to high water at mile marker 16. This 2 mile stretch of road closure caused interstate traffic to be diverted at the Wellington, Kansas exit (mile marker 19) through Wellington, which then returned to the interstate at the South Haven, Kansas  (mile marker 4) interchange.

Raging water along the Chikaskia River caused 5 teenagers to become trapped, as they were rafting down the river.  The water rescue that followed lead to 3 emergency workers ending up in the water along with the stranded teenagers. A volunteer firefighter then attempted to make an individual rescue, but lost his balance, and was swept under by the strong current.  The man later died from injuries sustained during the rescue.
Kansas Highway 49 north of Conway Springs and Kansas HIghway 42 near Suppesville were closed due to high water.
Flash flooding was reported 5 miles west of Winfield.

Cowley County Road 2 just east of Rock had water over the road.
Water was over county road 190th at Mustang.
Water was over County Road 40th at Timber Road and Upland Road.

Rapidly rising water along the Walnut River caused the Winfield Fairgrounds to flood.  This flood caused the rapid evacuation of thousands of campers who had come to claim thier spot for the annual Walnut Valley Festival. Muddy conditions caused by up to 3.50 inches of rainfall lead to many of the campers to be pulled or towed out of the effected area.  The water inundated the main grandstand and most of the stages, causing superfical damage but mainly caused some minor road damage.
Observer reported 6.50 inches of rainfall in Park City.

Almost 6 inches of rainfall overwhelmed the sewer and flood control systems in and around Park City.  This caused the closure of portions of 53rd Street, Hydraulic and Broadway through town.  Crews were called into to sandbag in and around The Park City Hall near 61st and Hydraulic.

Almost 10 inches of rainfall closed roads in the town of Maize and just to the south of Maize.  Numerous homes reported flooded basements.   The high waters forced the Maize USD 266 school district to dismiss classes early due to the lack of open roads.

Slow moving thunderstorms produced as much as 6 inches of rain across roughly the southwest quarter of Saline county during the late afternoon and evening hours. Consequently, localized flooding occurred. Water covered the Highway 140 and Reese Road intersection 3 miles east of Brookville, 6 inches of water covered Assaria Road 4 miles west of Assaria, and water covered Link Road just south of Water Well Road 7 miles southeast of Brookville. No known public or private damage occurred.

Rainfall amounts of 10.80 inches caused widespread flooding across Valley Center.  Hit the hardest was the Praire Lakes subdivision, where the large amount of rain caused the retention pond around the subdivision to rise rapidly and flood basements and stall cars. The Valley Center school district dismissed students early due to the high water and blocked access in and out of Valley Center.

Widespread heavy rains of 8 to 10 inches caused flooding of numerous county roads across Northern Sedgwick County. One fatality occurred to the south of the town of Sedgwick, near the 11200 block of North West, when a stalled motorist apparently attempted to flee his vehicle and was swept into the ditch by the fast moving water and drowned.

Nine to twelve inches of rainfall during the morning commute hours causing widespread street flooding of roadways up to 2 to 3 feet deep on the West side of the City of Wichita. Law enforcement officials reported 150 people were rescued from vehicles or evacuated because of the high water.  114 homes reported some type of surface flooding due to the heavy rainfall and sewers and sump pumps backed up into 141 more homes.  This unprecedented amount of rainfall mainly fell during a five hour period, reminding some of the Halloween Flood of 1998.  The large amount of rainfall caused the Cowskin/Calfskin Creek to once again come out of its banks, flooding homes in the Dells and Hidden Lakes Subdivision.  35 people were evacuated from the Park West Retirement home along the banks of the creek. Calls about stalled vehicles overwhelmed towing businesses across the city.
Rainfall amounts of 6.40 inches lead to widespread reports of water over county roads southwest of Wichita.
A National Weather Service employee measured 10.10 inches of rain.
A trained spotter reported 8.00 inches of rainfall for the storm.
Wichita Mid Continent Airport measured its all time greatest 24 hour rainfall total of 10.31 inches.
A local observer reported 5.25 inches of rain along Paradise Creek.  This caused roads to flood along the creek and washed out some small bridges.
An observer reported 9.81 inches of rain during the event.
Flooding along the Ninnescah River lead to evacuations in the Ponderosa area west of Belle Plaine.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured at Windom Elementary School.  Report courtesy KSN channel three.
Widespread wind gusts of 60 mph were relayed from across the county.
Widespread wind gusts of 60 mph were relayed from across the county.
Widespread wind gusts of 60 mph were relayed from across the county.
Widespread wind gusts of 60 mph were relayed from across the county.
A metal shed was knocked over on 700 road.
Wind damage was reported to several buildings.
Wind damage was reported to a home and several trees near the intersection of South Dakota Road and 1000 Road.
Trees were damaged between 1700 and 1800 Road near Anderson Road.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a barn.

Numerous roads were reported to have water over them including 167th Street West and Kellogg, 95th Street South and 263rd Street West and MacArthur at 135th Street West and 151st Street West. Rain of 2 to nearly 3.5 inches were reported in western Sedgwick County.
Minor street flooding was noted near Buhler and Pretty Prairie.  Water was over the roads in a few low lying locations.
Minor street flooding was being reported in McPherson.
Several county roads were closed due to the flooding of Cow Creek.
Several roads were closed due to flooding along Cow Creek.
A van was rolled over 3 miles south of Moran due to high winds.
Power outages occurred in Parsons due to downed power lines from snapped utility poles.
Power lines were downed in Stark due to high winds.
A power pole was snapped off 2 miles east southeast of La Harpe.
Several power lines were blown down due to high winds in Independence and Cherryvale.
A power line was blown down in Altoona due to high winds.
Law enforcement reported a large wind driven grass fire.  At least 8 fire departments responded to the fire.
Winfield ASOS reported a wind gust to 58 mph.
Wind gusts of 55 to 60 mph were reported near Howard.
The hail was mostly pea-sized but few up to the size of dime were reported.

One to three inches of snow fell across portions of the county leading to numerous traffic accidents.  Over 650 traffic accidents were reported in and an around the Greater Wichita area during the morning commute, with 36 injuries reported. One accident of note was a 5 to 6 car pileup near Park City along Interstate 135.

One to three inches of snow lead to numerous accidents across the county. A 56 year man died near El Dorado, KS., when he lost control of his pickup truck that rolled over.  Another accident, near the Augusta airport, injured two people as the vehicle they were driving left the highway and hit a parked recreational vehicle.  The driver of the vehicle had to be extricated and flown to a hospital in Wichita.
One to three inches of snow caused numerous accidents across the county.  Even with all the accidents only one injury was reported because of a car sliding off the road.

Scattered snow showers produced slick roads across portions of the county to the south of Iola. One accident involved a pickup pulling a travel trailer, that lost control on an icy bridge on Highway 169. The pickup lost control, overturned and caught fire. All 3 passengers were ejected from the pickup. One 34 year old man died and 2 others had serious injuries.

One to three inches of snowfall caused a total of ten accidents across portions of the county.  Two of the accidents were injury accidents when the vehicles they were driving overturned on slick highways.

Two to four inches of snow fell across portions of the county resulting in numerous accidents. One such accident killed a man, when he lost control of his car and hit a tree at a high rate of speed on a city street.
Two to five inches of snow lead to some accidents across portions of the county. One such accident injured a man, when his car slid out of control on Interstate 135 just north of the Lindsborg exit.

Three to four inches of snowfall caused several accidents across the county.  One such accident, injured a teenager, when his car slid into the path of a semi-tractor trailer along Kansas highway 96 near Haven.

Icy roads due to freezing drizzle and fog during the early morning hours resulted in an injury car accident one-quarter mile south of Arkansas Road on 1200 Street, about 4 miles south of Humboldt. A Humboldt woman lost control of her vehicle while traveling southbound on 1200 Street. She eventually struck a Humboldt man in his vehicle, and finally collided head-on with a Chanute man in his vehicle. Information courtesy of the Humboldt Union.

Icy roads due to freezing drizzle and foggy conditions during the early morning hours resulted in two injury accidents. The first one occurred just before 9 am when a 33 year old Belle Plaine man lost control of his pickup on a Highway 160 bridge about 12 miles east of Harper. The man was ejected from the cab after the pickup rolled several times. The second accident occurred about 20 minutes later at nearly the same location. A Harper man was driving a semi truck westbound on Highway 160 when he saw the previous accident ahead of him. When he started braking, the semi slid into the ditch. Information courtesy of the Harper Advocate.

One to two inches of snowfall lead to numerous accidents across portions of Southeast Kansas.  Five such accidents occurred across the county, but the most serious happened when a jeep with four teenagers slid into a fence and rolled over.  Only minor injuries occurred with the accident.

One to two inches of snow produced slick conditions across portions of Southeast Kansas.  One such such accident near Fredonia involved a  vehicles at a railrood crossing. Once the vehicle crossed the crossing it lost control and rolled into the ditch.  A passenger in the vehicle was injured and taken to the hospital.

Icy conditions due to light freezing rain and freezing drizzle aided in a fatal car accident shortly after 9 am just north of the Belle Plaine service center on the Kansas Turnpike. A 39-year-old Clearwater man and his 9-year-old son were traveling north on I-35 when the pickup rolled into the ditch after they lost control in the icy conditions. Sadly, the father died at the scene, while the boy sustained some injuries. Another accident occurred around 8:45 am when an SUV rolled near GKN Aerospace on Highway 81. About 30 minutes later, a semi-truck fell partially off a bridge on Highway 160, next to the Wellington Wal-Mart. Several other accidents, some with injuries, occurred across Sumner County on the 23rd due to the inclement weather. Information courtesy of the Wichita Eagle, Arkansas City Traveler and Wellington News.

Icy conditions due to light freezing rain and freezing drizzle aided in a fatal car accident around 9:30 am on Highway 77, 10 miles north of Winfield. A 37-year-old El Dorado man was injured when he lost control of the south-bound van and hit a tree, engulfing the van in flames. One of the passengers, a 19-year-old El Dorado man, was also injured. Sadly, the other passenger, a 61-year-old El Dorado man, was killed. Additionally, a Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks officer and a Highway Patrol Trooper sustained injures attempting to pull the 61-year-old El Dorado man from the van. Several other accidents, some with injuries, occurred on the 23rd across Cowley County due to the inclement weather. Information courtesy of the Wichita Eagle and Arkansas City Traveler.

Icy conditions due to light freezing rain and freezing drizzle aided in a three-vehicle accident on the 23rd shortly after 10 pm on I-135 just south of Crawford Street in Salina, resulting in two injuries. Information courtesy of the Salina Journal. Several other accidents were reported on I-70, but any other possible injuries remain unknown.

Icy conditions due to light freezing rain, freezing drizzle and light snow aided in an injury accident on K-96 a few miles south of South Hutchinson at 7:45 am on the 24th. A 55-year-old Yoder woman was westbound when her pickup hit a patch of ice, striking another pickup driven by a 32-year-old South Hutchinson man. Both were injured in the accident. Information courtesy of the Hutchinson News.

Icy conditions due to light freezing rain, freezing drizzle and light snow aided in a 24-year-old Hutchinson woman to lose control of her vehicle somewhere near Wichita on the morning of the 24th. The vehicle hit a fence and rolled once, injuring the woman. In another car accident, a 23-year-old Garden City man was injured on K-96 near 263rd Street around 10 am on the 24th, when another vehicle lost control and spun into his. Information courtesy of the Hutchinson News.

Icy conditions due to light freezing rain and freezing drizzle aided in a single-vehicle injury accident on I-135 north of Newton around 11:30 pm on the 23rd. The pickup lost control on the ice and rolled a few times in the median. Information courtesy of the Hutchinson News.
Measured by KSN Weather Lab Equipment at Bluestem Elementary School.
Measured by ASOS equipment at Strother Field Airport.
Measured by AWOS equipment at the Eureka Airport.

Lightning from a broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms sparked a house fire in the community of Colony during the predawn hours of the 27th. The residence was completely destroyed. Fortunately, no one was home at the time. Information courtesy of the Iola Register.
Law enforcement reported nickel sized hail.
Dime sized hail coverd the patio with 40 mph winds.
Sixty to sixty five mph winds were reported along Highway 160.
Quarter to golfball sized hail was reported.
A wind gust to 57 mph was reported at the Parsons Middle School.

Sleet accumulated to about one-half inch across the county, with a light glaze of ice underneath the sleet due to periodic freezing drizzle and freezing rain. Even though no reports of automobile accidents were received, it is probable that at least some occurred across the county due to the widespread slick road conditions.

Ice accumulated to about one-quarter inch across mainly southern portions of the county, due to periodic freezing drizzle and freezing rain. Light snow accumulated to about one-half inch. Numerous automobile accidents occurred countywide, but no reports of injuries were received.

One-quarter to one-half inch of ice accumulated across the county due to  periodic freezing drizzle, freezing rain and sleet. Additionally, one to two inches of snow accumulated on top of the ice, making for extremely slick road conditions. Numerous automobile accidents occurred countywide, but no reports of injuries were received.

One-quarter inch of ice and sleet accumulated across the county due to  periodic freezing drizzle, freezing rain and sleet. Additionally, light snow accumulations on top of the ice made for extremely slick road conditions. Numerous automobile accidents occurred countywide, one of which produced an injury. On the evening of the 26th, A Caney man was injured when he lost control of his vehicle on the icy road while driving southbound on Highway 169, north of County Road 3420 near Liberty. The vehicle went into the ditch and overturned. Information courtesy of the Independence Daily Reporter.

One-quarter inch of ice and sleet accumulated across the county due to  periodic freezing drizzle, freezing rain and sleet. Additionally, light snow accumulations on top of the ice made for extremely slick road conditions. Numerous automobile accidents occurred countywide, but no injuries were reported.

One-tenth to one-quarter inch of ice and sleet accumulated across mainly southeast portions of the county due to periodic freezing drizzle, freezing rain and sleet. Additionally, light snow accumulations on top of the ice made for extremely slick road conditions. Numerous automobile accidents occurred countywide, but no injuries were reported.

One-quarter inch of ice and sleet accumulated across the county due to periodic freezing drizzle, freezing rain and sleet. Additionally, a trace to one inch of light snow accumulated on top of the ice, making for extremely slick road conditions. Numerous automobile accidents occurred countywide, but no injuries were reported.

Around one-tenth of an inch of ice and sleet accumulation, and a dusting of light snow, led to very slick road conditions and numerous automobile accidents across the county. Tragically, a 93-year-old Burden man was injured badly on the 26th when he lost control of his vehicle on 112th Road, just west of 211th Road, sliding into the ditch. A short time later he died in the hospital. Information courtesy of the Winfield Daily Courier. A few Other injury accidents occurred across the county, but details are unknown.

A light glaze of ice due to freezing drizzle, sleet and light snow resulted in an injury accident on Highway 160 just west of Bluff Road. A 54-year-old Wichita man was traveling eastbound on Highway 160 when he lost control of his vehicle, entering the ditch, hitting a tree and finally overturning the vehicle. The passenger, a 46-year-old Wichita man, was also injured. Information courtesy of the Hutchinson News. Numerous other accidents likely occurred across the county due to the widespread slick conditions, but specific details are unknown.

A light glaze of ice due to freezing drizzle, sleet and light snow resulted in numerous automobile accidents across the county. One accident included one injury, but further details are unknown. Information courtesy of the Hutchinson News.
The tornado was reported just to the west of the intersection of highways 61 and 50. The tornado touched down in an open field with no damage reported.
Hutchinson tower observer reported the tornado just south of the airport runway and moving east. The tornado touched down in an open field with no damage reported.
A brief touchdown occured in open country near High Point road just southwest of Hutchinson.
A brief tornado touchdown occured in open country.

Law enforcement reported some tree branches and street signs blown down in Salina due to strong winds.
The Newton AWOS reported measured sustained winds of 40 mph for almost 40 minutes.
Law enforcement officials reported some minor damage from high winds.
Law Enforcement officials reported estimated sustained wind speeds of 40 mph.
Law Enforcement officials reported estimated sustained wind speeds of 40 mph.
The visitors dugout at Ray Bennett sofball field was destroyed by a thunderstorm wind gust along with a portion of the outfield fence.
The hail covered the ground.

Numerous power outages occurred from the high winds, likely due to downed power poles and lines. Meanwhile, a grass fire spread rapidly 2 miles southeast of Bunker Hill around 14:30 CST. Details remain unknown regarding the extend or severity of the fire.
High winds blew over semi-trucks on both I-70 and Highway 18.
At least one semi-truck was blown over on I-70. The roof of a shed at a lumber supply company in Ellsworth was blown off. The Ellsworth County Independent Reporter contributed to this report.
Very strong winds downed many power lines throughout the county, which caused several grass fires. Minor shingle and trim damage also occurred.

Very strong winds blew over 6 semi-trucks along I-70 in Saline County, with 2 injuries resulting. Numerous power lines were downed across the county as well, 18 of which went down along Schilling Road in South Salina. Numerous vehicle windows were broken out due to downed tree limbs. Some structural damage occurred as well, mainly confined to shingles, siding, windows and doors. At least one grass fire occurred, likely caused by the downed power lines.
Very strong winds downed several power lines throughout the county, which likely spawned at least 5 grass fires.

Measured by AWOS equipment at the McPherson Airport. The strong winds downed a few power poles and power lines across the county. A semi-truck overturned near the intersection of Highway 153 and 61. The McPherson Sentinel contributed to this report.
Very strong winds downed a few power poles in Peabody, and another in Hillsboro. A semi-truck was blown over on Highway 56 just outside of Marion.

Very strong winds inflicted roof damage to the Wiley building in downtown Hutchinson, blocking off main street for a time. Roof and shingle damage was reported 5 miles east of Sylvia, and two semi-trucks were blown over on Highway 50 between Yoder Road and K-96. At least six power poles were downed throughout the county, which caused several grass fires.
Periodic gusts likely approached 60 mph across the county.

Measured at the Wichita Mid-Continent Airport. Two-inch diameter tree limbs were downed near the Maple and West intersection in Wichita. Nearly 4,000 residents were without power for a time in Wichita due to downed power lines.
Periodic wind gusts likely exceeded 55 mph across the county.
Periodic wind gusts likely exceeded 55 mph across the county.

Quarter size hail occurred as well.
Winds to 70 mph also occurred.
A Channel 10 viewer reported a brief tornado touchdown in an open field.
The tornado moved southwest to northeast across the Lake Afton area, inflicting moderate damage to a residence. Two people were injured when their camper rolled at Lake Afton.
The tornado touched down briefly in an open field and then downed a few trees.
A hail covered the ground.
The hail was one inch thick on Highway 54.  This caused cars to slide off of the highway.
Quarter sized to golfball sized hail covered the ground between 70th and 80th road and Timber Road.
A semi tractor trailer was overturned a half mile south of the Highway 54 and Highway 169 intersection.

Heavy rainfall caused ponding of water on North Main Street in El Dorado. This ponding of water caused a car to slide off the road into a rain swollen culvert.  The heavy runoff carried the car 65 feet into a six by six culvert, where the driver became trapped and eventually drowned as water filled the car.
A brief touchdown occurred in open country.  No damage occurred.
The tornado briefly touched down in an open area and did not cause any damage.  The report came from the county sheriff.

Occasional light to moderate snow, with periodic bouts of heavy snow, affected mainly southeast portions of the county from the early morning hours on the 27th through the early morning hours on the 28th. Snowfall amounts ranged from a trace across northwest portions of the county, to around 4 inches across far southeast portions of the county. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow.

Occasional moderate to heavy snow affected much of the county from the early morning hours on the 27th through around the noon hour on the 28th. Snowfall amounts ranged from less than 4 inches across northwest portions of the county, to greater than one foot across mainly southern portions of the county. Ellsworth reported around 11 inches. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow. The weight of the snow caused a portion of a Kanopolis Lake gas station canopy to collapse. The Marquette Tribune contributed to this report.

Occasional light to moderate snow, with periodic bouts of heavy snow, affected mainly southeast portions of the county from the early morning hours on the 27th through the early morning hours on the 28th. Snowfall amounts ranged from a trace across northwest portions of the county, to greater than 6 inches across southeast portions of the county. Around 6 inches was reported in the city of Lincoln. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow.

Light snow affected the county during the morning and afternoon hours on the 27th, with occasional moderate to heavy snow developing by late afternoon and persisting through the late morning hours on the 28th. Snowfall amounts ranged from roughly 6 to 12 inches, with the least amounts across northwest portions of the county. Salina reported around 10 inches. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow. A number of relatively minor traffic accidents occurred across the county, including numerous slide-offs. The Salina Journal contributed to this report.

Light to moderate snow, with periodic bouts of heavy snow, affected the county from the predawn hours on the 27th through the early morning hours on the 28th. Snowfall amounts ranged from less than 4 inches across far northwest portions of the county, to over 15 inches across southern portions of the county. The cities of Great Bend and Ellinwood recieved around 16 inches. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow.

Light to moderate snow, with periodic bouts of heavy snow, affected the county from the predawn hours on the 27th through the mid morning hours on the 28th. Snowfall amounts ranged from roughly 12 to 16 inches across the county. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow, with visibilities occasionally dropping to one-quarter mile or less. One reported fatality occurred during the late evening hours on the 27th. A 71-year old Bushton man passed away while he was likely tending to his cattle. It remains uncertain if weather was the main contributing factor in his death. Additionally, a handful of stranded travelers were rescued by Lyons and Sterling Fire Department personnel. Lyons News contributed to this report.

Light to moderate snow, with periodic bouts of heavy snow, affected the county from the mid to late morning hours on the 27th, through the late morning hours on the 28th. However, areas of sleet accumulated across mainly southeast portions of the county during the day on the 27th. Snowfall amounts ranged from roughly 8 inches over far eastern portions of the county, to 12 to 18 inches elsewhere across the county. Inman received 18 inches, Windom and Marquette 15 inches, and McPherson 13 inches. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow, with visibilities occasionally dropping to one-quarter mile or less. The weight of the snow partially collapsed or damaged some roofs in McPherson, including a furniture store, a machinery and insulation plant, and the McPherson middle school. The Marquette Tribune, Salina Journal and Hutchinson News contributed to this report.

A wintry mix of light to moderate sleet, snow and freezing rain affected the county during the day on the 27th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to snow during the evening and overnight hours from west to east, and persisted into the afternoon hours on the 28th. Meaningful ice and sleet accumulations were confined to mainly southern and eastern portions of the county, where sleet accumulated over 2 and 3 inches in some places. Meanwhile, snowfall accumulations exceeded 8 inches over west and northwest portions of the county, where stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow, with visibilities occasionally dropping to one-quarter mile or less. Hillsboro received around 11 inches, and Marion received around 6 inches. Sadly, a 58-year-old Hillsboro woman was killed in a car accident due to the slick roads during the afternoon hours of the 27th. Two others were injured in the accident, which occurred about 7 miles north of Hillsboro on Indigo Road. The Newton Kansas, Salina Journal and Hillsboro Star contributed to this report.

A wintry mix of light to moderate sleet, snow and freezing rain affected the county from mid morning on the 27th into the overnight hours. The wintry mix eventually changed over to snow from west to east during the overnight hours on the 27th and early morning hours on the 28th, and persisted into the afternoon hours on the 28th. Sleet accumulated over 2 and 3 inches in some places, with many of those same areas also experiencing up to one-half inch ice accumulation from freezing rain. Snowfall accumulations on top of the sleet and ice ranged from 1 to 4 inches, heaviest over west and northwest portions of the county, where stout north to northeast winds resulted in some blowing and drifting of snow. Approximately 3 utility poles were downed across the county, along with some tree limbs due to the ice and wind.

Light to moderate snow, with periodic bouts of heavy snow, affected the county from the early morning hours on the 27th through the early afternoon hours on the 28th. However, southeast portions of the county received a wintry mix of snow and sleet through much of the day on the 27th, changing over to all snow during the evening and overnight hours. Widespread snowfall amounts ranged from roughly 12 to 20 inches across the county. Hutchinson received 16 inches, with western portions of the county reaching 20 inches. Southeast portions of the county received 7 to 12 inches of snow, on top of at least 1 to 2 inches of sleet. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow, with visibilities occasionally dropping to one-quarter mile or less. Three known injuries occurred in two automobile accidents due to the adverse road conditions. Unfortunately, an Arlington man died of a heart attack caused by shoveling snow. Paramedics were unable to reach him in a timely manner due to nearly impassable roads. Additionally, the heavy, wet snow caused a string of roof collapses and/or roof damage, including several businesses and a few schools. A canopy at the State Fairgrounds collapsed as well, along with some residential outbuildings and sheds. The Hutchinson News and Salina Journal contributed to this report.

A wintry mix of light to moderate sleet, snow and periodic freezing rain affected the county during the day on the 27th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to all snow from west to east during the evening and overnight hours, and persisted into the afternoon hours on the 28th. Meaningful ice and sleet accumulations were confined to mainly the eastern three-fourths of the county, where sleet accumulated over 2 to 3 inches in some places. Meanwhile, snowfall accumulations exceeded 12 inches over extreme west and northwest portions of the county, where stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow, with visibilities occasionally dropping to one-quarter mile or less. Total ice, sleet and snow accumulations over eastern portions of the county ranged from roughly 4 to 8 inches. Treacherous travel conditions lead to multiple accidents in and around Newton, some of which involved injuries, but none were critical. Portions of the roof of a Hesston plant collapsed underneath the weight of the heavy, wet snow. The combination of ice, snow and wind downed several power lines countywide. The Newton Kansan contributed to this report.

Light to moderate snow, with periodic bouts of heavy snow, affected the county from the early morning hours on the 27th through the early afternoon hours on the 28th. However, eastern and southern portions of the county received a wintry mix of snow and sleet through much of the day on the 27th, changing over to all snow from west to east during the evening and overnight hours. Snowfall amounts over western and northern portions of the county ranged from roughly 12 to 20 inches, while southern and eastern portions of the county received roughly 6 to 12 inches of snow on top of 2 to 3 inches of sleet. Cunningham received 15 to 20 inches of snow, while Kingman received 9 to 12 inches. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow, with visibilities occasionally dropping to one-quarter mile or less. Portions of the roof on a Kingman grocery store collapsed underneath the weight of the heavy, wet snow. Portions of the roof on the Kingman Activity Center collapsed as well. The Cunningham Courier and the Kingman Leader-Courier contributed to this report.

A wintry mix of light to moderate sleet and snow affected the county during the day on the 27th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to snow during the evening and overnight hours from west to east, and persisted into the afternoon hours on the 28th. Sleet accumulations across the county ranged from roughly 2 to 4 inches, with 6 to 15 inches of snow, highest over northwest portions of the county, accumulating on top of the sleet from the evening and overnight hours on the 27th and beyond. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow, with visibilities occasionally dropping to one-quarter mile or less. The combination of ice, snow and wind downed around 18 power poles across the county. Additionally, a couple businesses, one in Harper and the other just north of Attica received damage when portions of their roofs collapsed underneath the weight of the heavy, wet snow. There was one reported car port and front porch awning collapse across the county. The Harper Advocate and Hutchinson News contributed to this report.

A wintry mix of light to moderate sleet, snow and periodic freezing rain affected the county from the mid-morning hours on the 27th into the overnight hours. The wintry mix eventually changed over to all snow from west to east during the overnight hours on the 27th and early morning hours on the 28th, and persisted into the early afternoon hours. Sleet accumulations across the county ranged from roughly 2 to 4 inches, with freezing rain depositing one-quarter to one-half inch of ice over generally the eastern half of the county. Meanwhile, 3 to 8 inches of snow, highest amounts over far west and northwest portions of the county, accumulated on top of the ice and sleet. Total ice, sleet and snow accumulation measured about 7 inches across Wichita. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow, with visibilities occasionally dropping to one-quarter mile or less over mainly western portions of the county. Two people were injured when their vehicle slid off Kellogg and plunged into the Arkansas River. Additionally, portions of the Haysville Middle School roof was damaged due to the weight of the ice and snow. The Wichita Eagle and the Haysville Sun-Times contributed to this report.

A wintry mix of light to moderate sleet, snow freezing rain affected the county from the early to mid morning hours on the 27th into the overnight hours. The wintry mix eventually changed over to all snow from west to east during the overnight hours on the 27th and early morning hours on the 28th, and persisted into the afternoon hours. Sleet accumulations across the county ranged from roughly 2 to 4 inches, with freezing rain depositing one-quarter to one-half inch of ice over generally the eastern half of the county. Meanwhile, 2 to 8 inches of snow, highest over far western portions of the county, accumulated on top of the ice and sleet. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting of snow, with visibilities occasionally dropping to one-quarter mile or less over mainly western portions of the county.

A wintry mix of light to moderate sleet and freezing rain affected the county from mid morning on the 27th into the overnight hours, and into the early morning hours on the 28th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to all snow from west to east during the morning hours on the 28th, and persisted into the afternoon hours. Sleet accumulations ranged from 2 to 4 inches countywide, along with widespread ice accumulations of one-quarter to three-quarters of an inch due to freezing rain. Snowfall accumulations on top of the sleet and ice ranged from 1 to 5 inches, heaviest over western portions of the county, where stout north to northeast winds resulted in some blowing and drifting of snow. Unfortunately, a 22-year-old man was critically injured when the motorcycle he was driving hit a snow embankment on Highway 54 a few miles east of Andover. At least six other weather-related automobile accident injuries occurred across the county as well. The weight of the ice caused widespread tree damage, and numerous power poles and lines were downed as well, resulting in thousands of power outages. Additionally, various roofs (mainly flat-topped) sustained at least partial damage due to the weight of the ice, sleet and snow. The El Dorado Times, Augusta Daily Gazette, Rose Hill Reporter and Wichita Eagle contributed to this report.

A wintry mix of light to moderate sleet and freezing rain affected the county from the mid morning hours on the 27th through the early morning hours on the 28th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to all snow from west to east during the morning hours on the 28th, and persisted into the afternoon hours. Sleet accumulations ranged from 1 to 4 inches, highest over western and northern portions of the county. Additionally, ice accumulated one-quarter to three-quarters of an inch countywide due to freezing rain. Snowfall accumulations on top of the sleet and ice ranged from 1 to 3 inches, heaviest over western and northern portions of the county, where stout north to northeast winds resulted in some blowing snow and reduced visibilities during the morning hours on the 28th. The weight of the ice in concert with the wind downed numerous tree limbs across the county, along with some power lines and power poles. A 1250-foot radio tower collapsed near Winfield due to the weight of the ice. Power outages were numerous countywide.

A wintry mix of sleet and freezing rain affected the county from the early to mid morning hours on the 27th through the early morning hours on the 28th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to all snow from west to east during the morning hours on the 28th, and persisted into the afternoon hours. Widespread ice accumulations ranged from one-quarter to three quarters of an inch, with isolated 1 inch amounts. Total sleet and snow accumulations on top of the ice ranged from 1 to 3 inches. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in some blowing snow and reduced visibilities during the morning and afternoon hours on the 28th. The weight of the ice downed more than 80 power poles in the Piedmont area.

A wintry mix of sleet and freezing rain affected the county from the early to mid morning hours on the 27th through the early morning hours on the 28th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to all snow from west to east during the morning hours on the 28th, and persisted into the afternoon hours. Widespread ice accumulations ranged from one-quarter to three quarters of an inch, with isolated 1 inch amounts. Total sleet and snow accumulations on top of the ice ranged from 1 to 2 inches. The weight of the ice in concert with the stout winds downed some power poles, power lines and tree limbs across the county, which resulted in numerous power outages. The Independence Daily Reporter and Wilson County Citizen Paper contributed to this report.

A periodic wintry mix of rain, sleet and freezing rain affected the county from the early to mid morning hours on the 27th through the early morning hours on the 28th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to light snow from west to east for a relatively brief period during the morning and afternoon hours on the 28th. Widespread ice accumulations ranged from one-quarter to three quarters of an inch, especially over western portions of the county. Total sleet and snow accumulations on top of the ice ranged from a trace to 2 inches, highest over western portions of the county.

A wintry mix of freezing rain and periodic sleet affected the county from the early to mid morning hours on the 27th through the early morning hours on the 28th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to snow from west to east for a relatively brief period during the morning and afternoon hours on the 28th. Widespread ice accumulations ranged from one-quarter to three quarters of an inch. Total sleet and snow accumulations on top of the ice ranged from 1 to 3 inches, highest over far eastern portions of the county. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in some blowing snow, reducing visibilities during the morning and afternoon hours on the 28th. The weight of the ice in concert with the stout winds downed numerous tree limbs, along with some power poles and power lines, which resulted in widespread power outages. The Yates Center News and Wilson County Citizen Paper contributed to this report.

A wintry mix of rain and freezing rain affected the county from the afternoon hours on the 27th into the morning hours on the 28th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to snow during the mid to late morning and persisted into the afternoon hours on the 28th. Widespread ice accumulations ranged from a trace to one-quarter inch, highest across northwest portions of the county. Total snow accumulations on top of the ice ranged from 2 to 6 inches, highest over eastern portions of the county. Coffeyville received around 6 inches, and Independence around 4 inches. Stout north to northeast winds resulted in reduced visibilities in falling and blowing snow. Icy roads aided in numerous accidents and slide-offs, which caused 3 known injuries on Highway 166 13 miles west of Coffeyville. Additionally, the weight of the ice in concert with the stout winds downed several tree limbs and some power poles and power lines, causing various power outages. The Independence Daily Reporter contributed to this report.

A wintry mix of rain, freezing rain and sleet affected the county from the morning hours on the 27th into the morning hours on the 28th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to snow during the mid to late morning and persisted into the afternoon hours on the 28th. Widespread ice accumulations ranged from one-quarter to three-quarters of an inch, highest across northwest portions of the county. Total snow accumulations on top of the ice ranged from 1 to 5 inches, highest over east and southeast portions of the county. The weight of the ice in concert with the stout winds downed numerous tree limbs and some power poles and power lines, causing widespread power outages. The Wilson County Citizen and Independence Daily Reporter contributed to this report.

The community of LaHarpe lost water service on the 29th for a good portion of the day due to ongoing power outages. The Iola Register contributed to this report.

Heavy rainfall from numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours of the 26th produced widespread flooding across much of Rice county, with the exception of far northwest portions of the county. Numerous primarily rural roads remained submerged through early on the 28th. Some street flooding also occurred in Sterling on the 26th, and likely also occurred for other communities across the county. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unavailable.

Heavy rainfall from numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours on the 26th produced widespread urban and rural flooding across the county. Many locations received 3 to 5 inches of rainfall. Several roads were closed due to high water. Several minor water rescues were performed across the Wichita area. A home in the Haysville area suffered some water damage when its basement was flooded. Property damage amounts are conservative rough estimates.

Continued runoff from very heavy rainfall during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours on the 26th prolonged flooding across the greater Wichita area into the afternoon hours on the 28th, including areas along the swollen Cowskin Creek. Several rural and urban roads in and around the Wichita area were closed due to high water. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unknown.

Heavy rainfall from numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours on the 26th produced widespread flooding across much of McPherson county. Southeast portions of the county likely received the highest rainfall amounts. Numerous roads remained submerged and consequently closed through early on the 27th from the high water. Some street flooding occurred in McPherson and likely other communities as well. During the evening hours of the 26th, an injury accident occurred on Interstate 135 about 9 miles north of Highway 56 due to blinding heavy rainfall. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unavailable. The Hutchinson News contributed to this report.

Heavy rainfall from numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours on the 26th produced widespread flooding across much of Harper county. Rainfall amounts across the county ranged from 3 to 6 inches. Numerous roads were closed countywide. It is estimated that around 100 homes were flooded or received some form of water damage in the Anthony area, along with several other homes and businesses across the county. Portions of the elementary school and hospital in Harper were flooded. Three water rescues took place, one of which produced an injury near Third Lake Road when a vehicle attempted to cross a flooded roadway. Crop damage estimates are unknown, and property damage values are rough estimates. The Wichita Eagle, Harper Advocate, Anthony Republican and the Hutchinson News contributed to this report.

Very heavy rainfall from numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours on the 26th produced widespread flooding across much of Marion county. Rainfall rates on the evening of the 26th approached 2 inches per hour at Hillsboro. Numerous rural roads and some city streets remained submerged and consequently closed through early on the 28th. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unavailable.

Very heavy rainfall from numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours on the 26th produced flooding across mainly southeast portions of Kingman county. K-42 Highway near Norwich was down to one lane for a time on the evening of the 26th due to high water, and various other rural roads were closed. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unavailable.

Heavy rainfall from numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours on the 26th produced widespread urban and rural flooding across the county. Many locations received 3 to 5 inches of rainfall, with areas around Benton and Andover receiving over 6 inches of rainfall. Several rural and city roads were closed countywide due to high water. Nearly two dozen evacuations took place along Dry Creek near Santa Fe Lake about 3 miles northwest of Augusta, and also across portions of El Dorado. Several of those homes sustained flood damage, some of which was major, and several businesses in downtown El Dorado sustained water damage. The Wichita Eagle and Andover Journal-Advocate contributed to this report.

Heavy rainfall from numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours on the 26th produced widespread flooding across mainly northwest portions of Sumner county. Rainfall amounts exceeded 4 inches around Conway Springs. Numerous road closures likely took place due to high water, including K-49 Highway north of Conway Springs. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unavailable.

Continued runoff from very heavy rainfall during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours on the 26th prolonged flooding across the county into the early morning hours on the 29th, partly due to the moderate to major flooding along the swollen Walnut and Whitewater rivers and their associated tributaries. Several rural and some city roads around the county were closed due to high water. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unknown.

Continued runoff from very heavy rainfall during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours on the 26th prolonged flooding across Sumner county into the morning hours on the 29th, partly due to flooding along swollen rivers and creeks, including the Arkansas, Chikaskia, Ninnescah, and Slate, and their associated tributaries. Several rural and some city roads around the county were closed due to high water, including Highways 81 and 55 near the Ninnescah. A few homes were flooded south of 120th Avenue 2 miles west of Highway 81. Some water rescues were needed across the county. Property damage amounts are rough estimates. The Wellington Daily News contributed to this report.

The Cowley county fairgrounds in Winfield were inundated by portions of the swollen Walnut River, including some buildings on the grounds. Property damage amounts are rough estimates, and crop damage estimates are unknown. The Winfield Courier contributed to this report.

Heavy rainfall from numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours on the 26th produced widespread flooding across much of Greenwood county. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unavailable. The Yates Center News contributed to this report.
Straight-line winds blew over a grain bin east of Moundridge, and also damaged some farm equipment. The Moundridge Ledger contributed to this report.

Widespread 3 to 5 inch rainfall amounts likely occurred per radar estimates, producing both rural and city road closures due to high water. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unknown.

Numerous slow moving thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall during the afternoon and early evening hours on the 27th across much of Neosho county. Widespread 3 to 5 inch rainfall amounts likely occurred per radar estimates, producing several rural and city road closures due to high water. Thayer measured 4 inches of rainfall, with quite a bit of street flooding. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unknown.

Numerous slow moving thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall during the afternoon and early evening hours on the 27th across much of Montgomery county. Widespread 3 to 5 inch rainfall amounts likely occurred per radar estimates, producing several rural and some city road closures due to high water. Unfortunately, property and crop damage estimates are unknown.

Continued runoff from a couple heavy rainfall episodes from the 26th through the 30th produced river flooding along the Neosho River, and its associated tributaries across Neosho county. Several rural and some city roads were closed due to high water. The river flooding along the Neosho extended into the early mornings hours of May 2nd. Property damage amounts are rough estimates. The Chanute Tribune contributed to this report.

Continued runoff from a couple heavy rainfall episodes from the 26th through the 30th produced areal flooding across portions of Labette county, as well as river flooding along the Neosho River, and its associated tributaries. Several rural and some city roads were closed due to high water. Trailer homes along the Neosho River on Highway 400 near Parsons were partially submerged. Flooding extended into the evening hours of May 4th. Sadly, two people were killed sometime during the overnight hours of the 27th or the early morning hours of the 28th, after attempting to traverse a flooded low water bridge crossing in their vehicle due to the swollen Pumpkin Creek just east of Mound Valley on 15000 Road. The strong current swept their vehicle 200 feet downstream, likely trapping the two victims. The vehicle was found overturned and submerged in about 10 feet of water. Unfortunately, total property and crop damage estimates are unknown. The Independence Daily Reporter, Parsons Sun, and Coffeyville Journal, contributed to this report.

Damaging winds estimated to be 90 mph moved across most of Hutchinson causing extensive damage.  One of the worst hit areas was an area that was hit 8 days before by mircoburst winds in South Hutchinson (see June 7th, 2009), including damage to the same bus manufacturing plant, motel and storage facility.  This set of storms finished what the previous storms started, removing more walls and larger portions of the roof.  Three of the four buildings at a motel were considered a total loss.   Downtown Hutchinson also received significant damage, including removing a 100 foot by 30 foot section of roof to one business, and a portion of a roof to a loft.  A warehouse downtown suffered so much damage that it had to be demolished.  A power works building lost three of its overhead doors and an animal shelter had some roof damage. A large number of power of poles were also knocked down, especially near the state fairgrounds, where poles had to replaced from 17th to 30th Avenues on Plum Street.   30 to 40 percent of the city had tree limb damage.  The storm knocked out power to 7300 people.

A narrow swath of intense damage occurred, including uprooted trees, shattered car and building windows, at least three damaged irrigation systems, a damaged stock show trailer, structural and roof damage to several barns and homes, damage to various sheds and outbuildings, and devastating crop damage to soybeans, milo and corn. Additionally, a camper trailer was thrown into a field near Danville, and a railroad crossing was blown down just east of Danville. Property and crop damage monetary amounts incurred were $300 thousand and $1 million, respectively, but have been officially entered under the corresponding Hail Storm Data report. Freezing rain affected the county from the late night into early morning hours on the 23rd. Law enforcement reported up to one-quarter inch of ice accumulation and very slick roads countywide. Thereafter, patchy freezing drizzle occurred into the morning hours on the 24th, with only light additional ice accumulations. Numerous accidents were reported, two of which included injuries. A 42-year-old Hays woman lost control of her vehicle on an icy I-70 west of Russell. The vehicle entered the ditch and rolled. Additionally, a 64-year-old Platte City, Missouri man lost control of his vehicle on an icy I-70 east of Russell. The vehicle entered the ditch and rolled twice. A fatal accident occurred near the Dorrance exit on I-70, when a 39-year-old Houston, Texas man lost control of his vehicle on an icy overpass and overturned. The passenger, a 26-year-old Houston woman, was injured in the accident. Portions of this report were provided by the Salina Journal and Hutchinson News.

Two weather-related accidents were reported, one a couple miles south of Iola, and another south of Gas. It is unknown whether or not these accidents produced injuries. The cost to clear snow and ice across the county was about $38,000. The Iola Register contributed to this report.

A mixture of snow, sleet and freezing rain during the mid to late morning hours on the 24th changed to all snow during the afternoon hours, and continued into the early morning hours on the 25th. The sleet and snow was heavy at times. Snow accumulations ranged from 4 to 7 inches, highest across northeast portions of the county. The heavy snow in concert with strong and gusty northerly winds resulted in near blizzard conditions at times. A few minor vehicle accidents occurred across the county.

A mixture of snow, sleet and freezing rain persisted from the mid morning hours into the afternoon hours on the 24th. The wintry mix eventually changed over to all snow during the afternoon hours, and continued into the early morning hours on the 25th. The sleet and snow was heavy at times. Sleet accumulations reached up to 2 inches, with snow accumulations ranging from 4 to 8 inches, highest across southeast portions of the county. The heavy snow in concert with strong and gusty northerly winds resulted in near blizzard conditions at times. A few minor vehicle accidents were reported. The Parsons Sun contributed to this report.

Strong northwest winds lightly damaged the roof of a Hutchinson residence. Some other damage across Hutchinson includes a demolished 10 by 12 foot shed, a downed cable television line and a trash dumpster blown into a vehicle. Report courtesy of the Hutchinson News.

Freezing drizzle led to a few auto accidents across the county.  A pickup slid off of Kansas Highway 4 east of Hoisington, Kansas.  The driver and passenger were treated and released. Three other minor accidents occurred in and around Great Bend, Kansas.

Freezing drizzle led to numerous accidents on elevated roadways in and around Hutchinson, Kansas.  One accident occurred on US highway 56 east of Elinwood when two vehicles collided.  One driver had to be extricated from her car.  Both drivers were injured and taken to local hospitals. Another accident involved two vehicles, with 2 passengers sustaining numerous injuries and taken a local hospitals.

Freezing drizzle caused numerous accidents across the county.  A 42 year old Wichita, Kansas woman died in one such accident along Interstate 70 near Wilson, Kansas when the vehicle she was riding in slid into the path of an oncoming semi tractor trailer.  The driver was also seriously injured in the accident.

Freezing drizzle caused numerous accidents across the county.  During the afternoon three vehicles were involved in rollover accidents, with several other vehicles sliding off the road. One such accident along Interstate 135 involved at least five cars near Bridgeport, Kansas.

Overnight temperatures dropped to zero in Kingman.  This caused pipes to rupture at the VFW hall in Kingman.  The heat was inadvertently turned off which led to the pipes freezing.  The resulting pipes in the ceiling burst, cascading water into the kitchen.

The city of Wichita water department reported 160 calls of burst water lines or burst water meters. The extreme wind chills also led to numerous schools in and around Wichita to cancel on Friday, January 8th, as minus 20 degree wind chills made it unsafe for children to wait at the bus stops.

The tornado cycled very rapidly from a rope state to the classic tornado shape.  The tornado moved over open country and caused no damage.

A house was damaged with the roof being torn off of a house with 2 exterior walls being blown out (EF2 damage). Two garages were also destroyed and a riding lawnmower was removed from the garage and moved 100 yards downstream. Three people took shelter from the tornado in the basement and were unharmed.

Two semi tractor trailers were blown off of the Kansas Turnpike right at the state line as the tornado crossed the interstate. The tornado also caused significant tree damage as it moved northeast into rural Sumner County, Kansas.

Two supercell thunderstorms left a destructive swath of very large hail across portions of the county. The swath of hail was approximately 5 miles wide and 15 miles long, stretching from northwest of Goddard, Kansas through the western and southern half of Wichita, Kansas to near Rose Hill, Kansas.  Hail as large as softball and grapefruit size pounded roofs and cars along its path with over 35,000 claims turned into insurance agencies.   The hail made roofs look like a war zone, with holes big enough for people to stick their heads through.  Cars and golf courses were pot marked with large dents.  Some of the hail came through roofs, including the terminal at the Mid Continent Airport in Wichita.  Three commercial airliners were damaged and had to be towed to hangers for repairs.  The National Weather Service in Wichita suffered damage to its vehicles, including one hail dent that was almost 10 inches across.  One such hailstone 2 miles west of the National Weather Service office broke the state record for diameter, measuring 7.75 inches across (see separate entry).

A massive hailstone fell as part of a swath of hail that hit the county. (See the separate entry about the path of the storm). The hail stone that fell over West Wichita broke the state record for diameter at 7.75 inches.  However, the official weight and circumference were not able to be obtained until 15 hours after the stone had fallen. At that time, the stone weighed 1.1 pounds and had a circumference of 15.5 inches.  Members of a six-person State Climate Extremes Committee declared that the hailstone was the state's largest diameter stone to ever have fallen.

The Hutchinson News contributed to this report.

Periods of freezing drizzle produced icy roads countywide. Consequently, dozens of accidents were reported across the Wichita Area. Unfortunately, two accidents on the Kansas Turnpike proved fatal during the late evening on the 25th. One occurred near the Kellogg exit, the other near the Central Avenue exit. Each accident produced one fatality. Property damage amounts are rough estimates. The Wichita Eagle contributed to this report.
